candidates.name: order_id
candidates.verdict: NOT RECOMMENDED: High cardinality & even spread, but customer dashboard queries broadcast to ALL shards.

details.cardinality: High - Every order has a distinct ID.
details.distribution: Even - Random order UUIDs split evenly across chunks.
details.query_targeting: Scatter-Gather - Queries by customer_id must fan out to every shard.
details.monotonic: No (when UUID/random). Yes if auto-incrementing integer sequence.
details.read_performance: Poor for user-scoped reads; excellent only for single-order lookups.

candidates.name: customer_id
candidates.distribution: Uneven (Power Users & Wholesalers create jumbo chunks)
candidates.query_targeting: Excellent for Customer Queries (Targeted Single Shard)
candidates.verdict: ACCEPTABLE BUT RISKY: Excellent query targeting, but heavy buyers cause uneven shard size and jumbo chunk hotspots.

details.cardinality: High - Millions of unique customer records.
details.distribution: Uneven - Pareto distribution (80/20 rule): active buyers place 100x more orders.
details.query_targeting: Targeted - All orders for a given customer reside on one shard.
details.write_performance: Moderate - High-volume buyers route consecutive writes to a single shard.
details.read_performance: Optimal for customer history; risky for storage balance.

candidates.name: order_date
candidates.query_targeting: Good for Range Queries, Poor for Point Lookups
candidates.verdict: AVOID: Monotonically increasing values route 100% of current writes to the latest max-range shard (Write Hotspot).

details.cardinality: Moderate to High - Second/millisecond timestamp cardinality.
details.distribution: Severe Imbalance - All current inserts hit the single shard owning the max chunk ($maxKey).
details.query_targeting: Targeted for date ranges (e.g. quarterly reporting), scatter-gather for user queries.
details.monotonic: Yes - Time strictly advances, preventing write scale-out.
details.write_performance: Extremely Bottlenecked - Negates the primary benefit of sharding.
details.read_performance: Efficient for date range scans; terrible for concurrency.

candidates.name: hashed customer_id
candidates.query_targeting: Excellent for Targeted Lookups by Customer
candidates.verdict: BEST CHOICE (RECOMMENDED): Combines uniform write distribution with single-shard targeted customer queries.

details.cardinality: High - Preserves customer cardinality hashed over 64-bit space.
details.distribution: Even - Hash pseudo-randomness guarantees near 50/50 split across 2 shards.
details.query_targeting: Targeted - mongos hashes customer_id and routes directly to the owning shard.
details.monotonic: No - Sequential IDs hash to non-contiguous points.
details.write_performance: Optimal - Uniformly distributed across all shards in cluster.
details.read_performance: Optimal for customer dashboard and order history queries.

resharding.title: MongoDB 5.0+ Resharding Architecture (Activity 11.1)

steps.description: MongoDB validates cluster capacity: minimum 2x free disk space, verifies index existence on target key, and ensures no active long-running transactions.
A new hidden system collection is created with the new shard key and chunk ranges calculated across all destination shards.

steps.phase: 3. Initial Data Clone & Catch-up Oplog Streaming
steps.description: Donor shards stream baseline documents to recipient shards while live application writes continue unimpeded. Incoming oplog entries are applied in real-time.
When oplog lag drops below 2 seconds, MongoDB enters a brief (< 2s) critical section: writes are briefly paused, final oplog entries committed, and metadata flipped.
Config server updates cluster catalog pointing 'ecommerce.orders' to the new chunks. Donor collection files are asynchronously reclaimed.

limitations: Storage Overhead: Requires at least 2.5x the collection data size + indexes in free disk space during the operation.
Write Pause: Requires a brief write-block window (critical section) during final metadata cutover.
Single Active Operation: Only one resharding operation can run per cluster at any given time.
Cannot Reshard Time Series or Capped Collections: Specialized collection types cannot be resharded dynamically.
CPU & I/O Overhead: Sustained oplog replication and background index rebuilding impact concurrent production latency.
